newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FDA panel backs Glaxo smoking-cessation drug.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FDA panel backs Glaxo smoking-cessation drug.

text.p: A federal advisory committee on Thursday recommended that the Food and Drug Administration approve for marketing the Glaxo Wellcome Plc drug bupropion, in a sustained-release capsule, as an aid for smoking cessation.
It would be the first pill to be approved for smoking cessation. Other aids to stop smoking are patches, gum and nasal spray.

The FDA's Drug Abuse Advisory Committee found that bupropion was both safe and effective. Its findings are not binding on the FDA, but the agency usually accepts the recommendations of its expert panels.
Glaxo officials said the drug has been on the market since 1989 as a single-dose anti-depressant, and since earlier this year as a staged-release anti-depressant.
It is the staged-release version that will be considered by the FDA as an aid for quitting smoking.
The Glaxo officials said the pill would be the first non-nicotine treatment used as an aid to smoking cessation.
Bupropion, marketed for anti-depressant use as Wellbutrin, has caused seizures in some depressed patients, but Glaxo officials said trials of the drug for smoking cessation showed no seizures.
FDA advisory committee members said they would recommend special labeling for the drug when it is prescribed by doctors for smoking cessation. In addition, counseling would be offered.
Glaxo said it would recommend a dose of once or twice a day, possibly in conjunction with the use of other aids to stop smoking.
The Glaxo officials said they got the idea for using the drug for smoking cessation because many of the depressed patients who were given it and who smoked wound up stopping smoking.
